title: Malay stage rules: affix gates, whole-word exemptions, look-alike roots, register pairs and disallowed forms
authority: Charter section 5 (affix order; ber- has no nasal sound changes, edited 13 Nov 2026 at Sam's request, R7); docs/stage-2-plan.md section 3; Sam's answers of 13 Nov 2026 in docs/stage-2-decisions.md (R3, R4, R7) and ledger Journal rows 130 to 132; Sam's build step 2 instruction of 13 Nov 2026. Readers: Cikgu Sensai language_checks.py (now) and Kata-Kata tools/affix-guard.mjs (build step 3).

format.summary: Plain JSON, UTF-8. Every Malay form is lower case and compared with whole words (tokens of letters, with internal hyphens or apostrophes kept). A reader must ignore keys it does not know and must not edit this file to make content pass: a change needs Sam's approval, recorded in the ledger Journal or HANDOFF.md.
format.affix_gates: List of {family, chapter, ledger_tags, detect, note}. family is the rule name used in messages. chapter is the first chapter in which the family may be used productively. ledger_tags are the ledger 'Affix tag' tokens that name the family (a tag such as 'meN- -i' names two families; the form then needs every gate). detect describes the shape test used when the ledger has no family tag for the word: 'shape' families are found from spelling alone, 'tag-only' families only from the ledger tag. enforced_by says which rule set enforces it: 'stage1' rules are the Stage 1 checks kept unchanged; 'stage2' rules are the stage-aware check below.
format.stage_aware_rule: A word whose family has a 'stage2' gate passes only if (1) the unit's chapter is at or after every gate of the word's families, and (2) the word's own ledger row, or for a regular Stage 1 derivation (di-, -nya, -kah) the row of its base, is placed at or before the unit's chapter. Placement is read from the ledger 'Kata-Kata place' column only: the lowest 'ChN' after removing notes 'moved from ChN', 'reviewed in ChN', 'reused ChN', 'was ChN' and 'waits for ChN'; a retired row is never placed. A word in a ‹…› mention listed with its source in curriculum/malay-mentions.json is not taught vocabulary and is not checked.
format.family_resolution: 1. A word in lookalike_roots, or in whole_words at or after its chapter, has no family. 2. If any ledger row of the word has an Affix tag other than 'root' or blank (for example '-an', 'lex', 'chunk', 'ber-'), that tag decides the families. 3. Otherwise (no row, blank tag, or 'root') the shape tests decide; this is how rows tagged 'root' that are really ter- forms (L-0619 tertinggal, L-0621 terlepas, L-0644 terlupa) are still gated. 4. A ter- word is the chapter 6 superlative only if it is in ter_superlatives or it has no ledger row of its own and its base is an adjective; every other ter- word is the accident or unplanned-state family.
format.shape_tests: ber-: begins with ber, or with bek or bel (be- and bel- spellings). meN-: begins with me followed by a consonant. -kan: ends in kan, longer than 5 letters, and the word without kan (and without a meN-, di-, ber- or ter- prefix, nasal changes reversed) is a known ledger or Kata-Kata form of 3 letters or more; so makan, ikan, bukan and akan are roots. -i: tag-only for bare words (selesai, pandai and kaki are roots); with a meN- or di- prefix, the word without the prefix and without its final i must be a known form of 3 letters or more, so membeli, mencari and mengisi are not -i forms. ter-: begins with ter and the rest is a known form of 3 letters or more (terima, terus and teruk are roots).
format.whole_words: List of {form, chapter, ledger_id, reason}. Lexicalised or allow-listed whole words that look affixed. Each is a whole word at its own chapter (equal to its ledger row's chapter); before that chapter the normal rules apply. Never a family exemption for any other word.
format.ter_superlatives: The chapter 6 lexical superlatives, whole words from chapter 6. They never open the accident ter- family.
format.lookalike_roots: Roots that only look affixed (beri, merah, mesti ...). Classification only: they do not create ledger rows or chapter placements. Sam's local additions also stay in curriculum/malay-roots.json, which must remain a subset of this list.
format.register_pairs: List of {spoken, standard, from_chapter, decision}. In any unit whose chapter is from_chapter or later (and in unplaced units), the spoken form fails unless the standard form has been taught earlier in vocabulary or a model and the spoken form has been taught with an explicit 'spoken' label. Multi-word forms match as whole phrases. register_notes records Sam's decisions on how a pair is presented.
format.particles: List of {form, decision, rule, not_particle}. Recognition particles: allowed in prompts and listening once placed, never required in a test answer key («lah» as a word or as an ending on a known form with no ledger row of its own, except the not_particle words; «kan» as a word). A key that must name the particle quotes it as a ‹…› mention.
format.disallowed_forms: Map form -> Malaysian form to use. Matched as whole words, also inside hyphenated words; a form of two words («tanda tangan») is matched as the two words in that order. Fails everywhere, including mentions, except inside a ‹…› mention whose source in curriculum/malay-mentions.json says 'do not use'.

affix_gates.note: Possessive or definite -nya on a known word.
ke- + number (keempat); pertama is a whole word.
seekor, sebiji, sebuah: se- with a counter; the counter's own chapter is checked (chapter 8). Time nouns (seminggu) follow their base's chapter (4).
di- + a known verb root from chapter 9 (dibaca, dibeli). The Stage 1 rule stays; a di- form that also carries -kan or -i needs that gate too (dibenarkan: 12, and its row is chapter 13).

No nasal sound changes (charter, R7). Spelling variants: be- before a root starting with r (berehat, berenang) or whose first syllable ends in -er (bekerja); bel- only in belajar, a chapter 2 whole word.
me-, mem-, men-, meng-, meny-, menge- with nasal changes (tulis -> menulis, sewa -> menyewa, cas -> mengecas).
Selected -kan families (simpankan, hidupkan). meN-...-kan needs both 11 and 12. Not a politeness ending; kan the particle is separate (see particles).

affix_gates.detect: tag-only for bare words; shape after meN- or di-
affix_gates.note: Selected -i families (baiki, membaiki, hubungi). A final i is not -i (membeli, mengisi).
Accidental or unplanned-state ter- (terjatuh, tertinggal, terkunci). Ability, success and idiom readings are outside Stage 2.

whole_words.reason: The only bel- spelling of ber- (charter section 5, R7); a lexicalised chapter 2 word.
Question word, lexicalised (Sam, 12 Nov 2026: kenapa, mengapa and apa sebab are equivalents).
Root that looks like ber- + sih.
Root that looks like meN- (Dunia, primes chapter 6).
ber- with the be- spelling (first syllable of kerja ends in -er); a rule, not an exception (R7).
ber- with the be- spelling before r (rehat).

particles.rule: Recognition; production optional; never required in a test answer key. Written joined to a word («takpelah», «tidak mengapalah») it is read as that word + lah from the chapter of the particle's own ledger row (17), only when the rest is a known form and the whole word is not a ledger word or a not_particle word (derivation rule '-lah', like -kah).
particles.not_particle_note: Whole words that end in -lah on a known form but contain no particle (ada + lah, masa + lah are not their sources).

particles.rule: Recognition (confirmation particle, not the suffix -kan); production optional; never required in a test answer key.
